purpose: Every place where the live App Router surface and docs/route-register.json disagree. scripts/route-register-correspondence.test.ts checks which routes exist; scripts/route-gate.ts (pnpm gate:routes) checks the methods they export, the status their redirects emit, the storage buckets their prefixes name and the (route, state) pairs a browser test proves. Both fail when a divergence appears that is not listed here, and fail when a listed one is fixed or misdescribed, so this file cannot quietly drift from reality in either direction.
notAnApproval: Listing a divergence records it; it does not bless it. The register is the binding response-contract authority, so an unregistered live endpoint has no declared auth mode, response contract or policy. Each entry names what is missing and what closing it needs.
unregisteredServerActionsNote: A server action is a live mutation surface that the route register does not describe: Next.js exposes it at a generated endpoint the App Router never shows, so none of the route checks above can see it and a second one could appear without anything noticing. G8.5 asks that every live surface match its register, so the surface is held as a ledger instead, compared in both directions by scripts/route-register-correspondence.test.ts. One exists today and it is unregistered on purpose, with the reason written in the file itself. Adding another fails until it is recorded here; deleting this one fails as a stale row.

unregisteredServerActions.why: The Embryo domain's Tier-2 acknowledgement (design §1.5). Its own header states the reasoning: "A server function rather than a route: it is reachable only from this domain's own pages and needs no register row, and Next.js checks the request origin before it runs." It writes one httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie whose value is a keyed digest of the account id and the current auth session id, with no Max-Age; it writes nothing to the database and nothing to device storage, and a new auth session cannot verify it. So it mutates no durable state and carries no authority a route would have to gate.
unregisteredServerActions.closing: Nothing. This row is not a defect and is not waiting on anything — it records a deliberate choice so that the NEXT server action has to be argued for rather than merely added. If one is ever given durable writes or authority of its own, it belongs in the register as an endpoint instead of in this list.

methodDivergenceNote: 2026-10-01 NEXT-RELEASE: api.export now exports the registered GET and POST, so the former GET-only method row is stale and removed. This is verb correspondence only. The POST consumes actual current account operation/CSRF proof but refuses before create while the provider capability is unconfigured. Cookie-present GET performs the read-only current-origin check; no-cookie GET still performs the original synchronous export. Public action presentation, complete READY/member metadata, open-ready, delivery/provider proof and thirteen unsupported account classes remain unbuilt or explicitly refused. docs/account-archive-orchestration.md records the exact partial continuation; no G5.6 or acceptance credit follows from method equality.
redirectStatusDivergenceNote: Empty on purpose, and checked in both directions so it cannot stay empty through a regression. The register pins all ten legacy aliases to expectedStatus 308. Eight are pages calling permanentRedirect. /signup and /login were next.config.ts entries with permanent: false, which emits 307 — a 307 asks the browser back to the dead path every time, so the alias never retires. Both now read permanent: true.
kindDivergenceNote: Empty since 2026-09-28, and still checked in both directions. /withdraw/request was the one registered page literal served by a route.ts. The owner decided that evening that the register describes it as what it is: rights.withdraw-request, an HTML endpoint with its own response contract (rights-interstitial-v1), and rights.withdraw now pins its segment to session alone. Its one-script Content-Security-Policy is what makes the URL-fragment rule provable, which a React page cannot keep.

storageBucketDivergence.why: Evidence for claim and appeal review, declared with service-only access and application envelope encryption on top of provider at-rest encryption. Nothing creates it because the claim and appeal surfaces it serves are unbuilt.
storageBucketDivergence.closing: Created with the declared policies and the document-specific data key when evidence ingest is built.

provenRouteStatesNote: The (route, state) pairs a browser test title proves today, out of the 288 the register requires. scripts/route-gate.ts recomputes this list from e2e/**/*.spec.ts titles and fails if it differs in either direction, and UNPROVEN_ROUTE_STATE_PAIRS in that script holds the remainder. A title proves a pair when it names the registered route path and the state id as separate, non-overlapping, whole tokens, so "empty-history" does not prove "empty" and a state id appearing only inside the path proves nothing.
unhashableAttestationFieldsNote: Request fields the register requires that nothing can honestly produce, because the artifact they attest to does not exist. D-083. `policy.jurisdiction` appears nowhere in this repository outside docs/route-register.json — not in src/, not in the docs, not in a test — so there is no published version to name and no body to hash; these bodies carry a plain `jurisdictionCode` instead. Owner decision 2026-09-13: record the divergence and keep the code, rather than author a legal artifact to satisfy a field or drop a commitment the brief made about proving which jurisdiction a person accepted under. scripts/route-gate.ts compares this list with the register in BOTH directions, so a sixth route declaring the fields fails until it is recorded here, and the day the artifact is authored and the fields are really served, every row here fails until it is removed.
unreadRequiredHeadersNote: Required headers that no source module reads remain checked in both directions. Owner decision 2026-09-22 removes both extra headers only from the embryo chunk route, whose strict cookie, live account/session, Origin and database chunk identity provide the approved authority. Owner decision 2026-09-28 does the same for api.evidence-chunk: each claim document chunk sequence is reserved once, in the transaction that rechecks the session, the claim, the cumulative bytes and the server-computed SHA-256, so the register no longer requires a separate one-time chunk nonce there.
taskDepthCeilingDivergenceNote: Resolved by owner decision 2026-09-22: T9 has a ceiling of six in-app click/submit actions with the registered confirmation exclusions. Mailed-link and typed-URL entry events are recorded separately. The brief, register, rubric and human protocol now use the same units. The gate still compares the empty divergence ledger in both directions.
